sentences.text: In 2024, Romania's top court cancelled a presidential election.
Who can vote? Romanians from 18 with an ID card, even abroad or by post.
You get two ballots, each a booklet of party lists. Stamp VOTED in one party's box.
Parties need 5%, then seats follow the vote.
They fill two chambers, 331 deputies and 134 senators, who pass the laws.
The president names a prime minister, who needs 233 votes in parliament.
The president, elected directly, leads defence and foreign policy. The court cited foreign interference, and Nicușor Dan won the rerun.
In 2024, the Social Democrats came first with 22%, and seven parties got in.
In 2026, parliament ousted the prime minister. The president's fourth pick, Luca Niculescu, won 280 votes.
Should a court ever be allowed to cancel an election?
